abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dihydroceramide desaturase (DES1) plays key roles in many cellular biologies and pathologies, underscoring a need for DES1 inhibitors, both as research tools and potential therapeutic agents. In this study, we have evaluated the recently reported novel DES1 inhibitor PR280 and its newly synthesized analog PR280b. We find that while both compounds are potent in vitro and in situ DES1 inhibitors, they induced broader changes in cellular sphingolipids, most notably increased ceramide levels, that go beyond DES1 inhibition and had modest effects on DES1-driven biologies including anchorage-independent survival, apoptosis, and autophagy. Overall, although this limits the direct utility of PR280 as a specific DES1 inhibitor, this highlights the potential of this scaffold for further inhibitor development aimed at maintaining the DES1 inhibitory activity while reducing off-target effects.
